title: Responsivity of a silicon photodiode
caption: Each absorbed photon gives at most one electron, so the current per watt, R = ηλe/hc, grows with wavelength (longer-wavelength photons each carry less energy). With η = 0.8, R = 0.55 A W⁻¹ at 850 nm. Beyond λ = hc/E_g = 1107 nm photons cannot cross silicon's band gap and the response stops.
alt: Responsivity in amps per watt against wavelength, a straight line rising from 400 nanometres to a cut-off at about 1100 nanometres, with 0.55 at 850 marked.
description: R = η × λ (nm) / 1240 A W⁻¹, with η = 0.8.
Cut-off: 1240 / 1.12 eV = 1107 nm; no response beyond it.
Real silicon diodes fall off before the cut-off because absorption becomes weak near the gap (not shown).
